Architecture Diagram

The application is a server-rendered catalog management website with optional Azure-backed storage and authentication. Its primary request path runs through MVC controllers and services to Entity Framework and SQL Server.

Data Storage & External Services

Catalog items, brands, and types use SQL Server through Entity Framework. A local SQL Server LocalDB connection is configured for plain .NET execution, while Compose and environment configuration support container/deployed settings. Images use local files in the mock implementation or Azure Blob Storage when enabled. Azure Active Directory/OpenID Connect, Application Insights, and Redis-backed session state are optional integrations.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Autofac registers a catalog service, image service, SQL connection factory, and a singleton hi-lo ID generator.
  • ICatalogService has database-backed and in-memory mock implementations selected by configuration.
  • Entity Framework maps catalog item relationships directly to catalog type and brand; there is no separate repository layer.

DTOs & Contracts

No separate API DTO layer or OpenAPI/Swagger specification was found. MVC actions bind catalog create/edit form submissions to the mutable CatalogItem model; list actions return a PaginatedItemsViewModel. The upload action returns an anonymous JSON object containing name and url. Entity and persistence structure is documented in data-architecture.md.

Communication Patterns

The browser communicates synchronously with MVC actions over HTTP. Controllers call ICatalogService and IImageService in-process; the EF6 context accesses SQL Server directly. Image storage is local in mock mode or uses the Azure Blob SDK when configured. Authentication uses OWIN cookies and OpenID Connect with Microsoft Entra ID when enabled. No asynchronous message broker use, gateway aggregation, service discovery, circuit breaker, or explicit retry policy was found. TLS is not enforced globally in the application; the configured local logout redirect uses HTTPS.

Catalog create/edit/delete actions are protected with [Authorize]. Public catalog browsing and the image-upload action do not show an authorization attribute. The OIDC AuthenticationFailed callback redirects to an error page.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports maintaining an e-commerce product catalog, including product classification, brand assignment, stock information, and product images. Catalog browsing is available to users, while catalog changes require authentication.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalog ManagementProduct listing with price, stock, and image referenceBelongs to one CatalogType and one CatalogBrand
CatalogTypeCatalog ManagementProduct categoryGroups many catalog items
CatalogBrandCatalog ManagementProduct brandLabels many catalog items

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedMVCCatalog ManagementCatalogItem, CatalogType, CatalogBrandSQL Server, local or Azure image storage, optional Microsoft Entra ID

There are no separate business services or cross-context data exchanges. The MVC application is the source of truth for its catalog entities.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the Catalog

  1. A user opens the catalog listing.
  2. CatalogController requests a page from ICatalogService.
  3. The database-backed service loads items with their brand and type; mock mode instead uses in-memory preconfigured data.
  4. The controller resolves image URLs and renders the catalog view.
  5. A detail request loads one catalog item and returns either the detail page or a not-found response.

Workflow 2: Maintain a Catalog Item

  1. An authenticated catalog manager opens the create or edit form.
  2. The manager may upload an image through PicController; the action decodes the content and accepts JPEG, PNG, or GIF images.
  3. The create/edit action validates the bound CatalogItem model. Model annotations validate required name, price range/format, and stock thresholds.
  4. CatalogService allocates an identifier for a new item, then persists the item through Entity Framework; edits update the entity and deletes remove it.
  5. If an image was uploaded, the selected image service stores or copies it to local or Azure storage.
  6. Successful writes redirect to the catalog listing; invalid models return the form with validation errors.

Workflow 3: Seed Catalog Data

At application startup, CatalogDBInitializer seeds catalog types, brands, and items from built-in data or optional CSV customization files. It creates/uses SQL sequence values for identifiers and initializes images when configured.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No cross-service business composition was found. The application accesses SQL Server and image storage directly through its own services. The image service may use Azure Blob Storage when enabled; otherwise the local/mock implementation resolves images from the application Pics directory.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Manager as "Catalog Manager" participant MVC as "Catalog Controller" participant Image as "Image Service" participant Catalog as "Catalog Service" participant DB as "Catalog Database" Manager->>MVC: Submit item details MVC->>MVC: Check model validation alt Item details are valid opt Image was uploaded Manager->>Image: Submit image Image->>Image: Decode and check image format Image-->>Manager: Temporary image URL end MVC->>Catalog: Create or update catalog item Catalog->>DB: Save catalog record DB-->>Catalog: Save completed Catalog-->>MVC: Operation completed MVC-->>Manager: Redirect to catalog else Item details are invalid MVC-->>Manager: Return form with validation errors end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Catalog item name is required. Price must be in range and use no more than two decimal places; stock and threshold values are constrained to nonnegative bounded ranges.
  • Each catalog item requires a catalog type and brand.
  • Only authenticated users can create, edit, or delete catalog items.
  • Image upload accepts content decoded as JPEG, PNG, or GIF; the storage implementation depends on configuration.
  • New database-backed catalog IDs come from SQL hi-lo sequences; mock mode assigns incrementing in-memory IDs.
  • EF6 operations save changes through the catalog service. No multi-service saga, event choreography, audit trail, or compensating transaction was identified.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The project targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses the classic ASP.NET MVC 5 and Entity Framework 6 stack. Several dependency families are older, including IdentityModel 5.6.0, Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.2, and log4net 2.0.12; the security assessment also identified medium-severity advisories for IdentityModel token packages and log4net.

Notable Observations

  • packages.config is the dependency source; the project does not use central package management or a lock file.
  • Azure Key Vault and configuration-builder packages are present, but the application enables those integrations through configuration.
  • Redis is declared for optional session storage; no general-purpose application cache was identified.
  • No test-scoped packages or separate test project were found in the target solution.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The data layer contains three catalog entities persisted through Entity Framework 6 to SQL Server. It has no separate repository interfaces or general-purpose application cache.

No database profile-specific migration framework such as Flyway or Liquibase was detected. The initializer seeds catalog types, brands, and items from predefined data or CSV files and creates SQL sequence objects from checked-in scripts.

Entity Model

CatalogDBContext maps the CatalogItem relationships to required CatalogType and CatalogBrand foreign keys. Entity definitions are in Models/CatalogItem.cs, Models/CatalogType.cs, and Models/CatalogBrand.cs; mapping is in Models/CatalogDBContext.cs. There is no repository interface; CatalogService accesses CatalogDBContext directly.

Caching Strategy

No application-level catalog cache was found. Redis is available through the optional Microsoft.Web.RedisSessionStateProvider configuration, but the provider configuration is commented out by default. Azure Blob Storage holds image files when the Azure image service is selected; it is persistent object storage rather than a cache.

Data Ownership Boundaries

All catalog entities are stored by the MVC application in a single SQL Server database. There are no separate services or cross-service database calls; controllers access catalog data through the application service and EF6 context. Image bytes are stored either in the local Pics directory or in the pics Azure Blob container.
